title: ISic020938. Graffito of Thexenos on a black-glaze kylix from Syracuse
body:
Text encoding: Valentina Mignosa
1Θέξενος

Text encoding: Valentina Mignosa
1ΘΕΞΕΝΟΣ

Facsimile Images

Apparatus criticus

  • Text after photograph (Guzzardi 2012, 174 fig. 16).

English translation

Valentina Mignosa

Thexenos.

Italian translation

Valentina Mignosa

Thexenos.

commentary

The graffito preserves the personal name Θέξενος. Guzzardi compares this form with the well-attested name Θεόξενος. The name Θέξενος is listed by Pape and Benseler (1911, 274 s.v.) and is independently attested at Delphi in SGDI II 2156, l. 6, as Θέξενος Φιλαιτώλου. The use of Ξ for /ks/ is particularly significant for assigning the graffito to the Syracusan alphabet since contemporary Attic writing represented /ks/ with the digraph ΧΣ (see for comparison Dubois, IGDS I, no. 96). The forms of the other letters, including theta, are also compatible with the Syracusan alphabet, although they are not independently diagnostic. The palaeography therefore favours a Syracusan attribution for the inscription, despite the probable Attic manufacture of the kylix. An ownership function is plausible for an isolated personal name scratched on a drinking vessel, but it remains uncertain. Guzzardi regards the vessel as contemporary with the phase of the Ionic temple dated to c. 490–480 BCE, although it was recovered as residual material together with Roman-period finds in a fill layer east of the excavation and outside the municipal building. The same archaeological complex also preserves three signs incised on architectural blocks, recorded as ISic004516 (sigma, or possibly mu), ISic004517 (pi) and ISic004518 (theta).
